info.title: SMB Sales Boost API
info.description: REST API for SMB Sales Boost - a B2B lead generation platform that helps you find growing local businesses to reach out to: small and medium businesses across the United States showing growth signals such as new websites, new social profiles and fresh online activity (newly registered businesses are one subset). Search, filter, and export leads with comprehensive company data including contact information, location, and AI-enriched categories. API access requires a Starter, Growth, Scale, Platinum, or Enterprise subscription plan, including during the 14-day free trial. New users can purchase a subscription (or start a free trial) entirely via API with POST /purchase (no web signup required); the API key is emailed after checkout. A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server is also available at https://smbsalesboost.com/mcp for AI assistant integration - see https://smbsalesboost.com/docs/api/mcp-server for details. Every operation that uses an API key can also return 401 unauthorized (missing, invalid or revoked key), 403 forbidden (no active or trialing paid subscription), 429 (more than 600 requests per minute per key) and 503 service_unavailable (temporary; retry after the Retry-After delay).

tags.name: Enrichments
tags.description:
Enrich a list of website URLs. Each URL is checked against the SMB Sales Boost database first; anything not already there is fetched live. We never add the URLs you submit, or the results we find for them, to our lead database, which we keep curated so it stays clean and focused on high-quality leads.

**Pricing.** 1 credit for a URL in the database you have not bought before (this includes its buying signals and category enrichments). 0.1 credit for a URL fetched live. 0 credits for a URL you have already exported, one we got no data for, and one without the contact details you asked for.

**A URL found in the database is never fetched live**, so lowering `databaseMatchPercent` does not let you buy database records at the live price.

**Runs are asynchronous.** Submitting returns a run id immediately; a large list can take hours. Poll `GET /enrichments/{id}` until `status` is `completed` or `partial`, then call `/download`.

**Credits are charged in two stages.** Database matches are charged as soon as they are matched; live results are charged when the file is published. `credits.final` tells you whether the total is settled.

post.summary: Start a subscription purchase or free trial
post.description:
Create a Stripe Checkout session for a subscription entirely via API. No web signup, onboarding or API key is needed. The 201 response carries checkoutUrl (open it in a browser to pay or to start the trial), expiresAt, plan, a trial object and a message. It does not return a claim token or the API key: the API key is emailed to the address you supplied once checkout is complete. If that address already has an SMB Sales Boost account, the purchase is first confirmed from an email sent to that address, and the key follows once it is confirmed.

Free trial: Starter, Growth and Scale start with a 14-day free trial by default. trial defaults to true; only the JSON boolean false skips the trial and charges the plan price at checkout. Platinum and Enterprise never trial. During a trial a payment method is required, nothing is charged at checkout, the trial includes 50% of the plan's monthly credits, and the plan price is charged automatically when the trial ends unless the subscription is cancelled first. One trial per person: this endpoint checks the email address (see trial.eligible and trial.reason in the response), and the payment method is checked after checkout, where a checkout whose card already had a trial is cancelled without a charge. All charges are final; there are no refunds.

Rate limited to 5 requests per hour per IP.

get.description:
Search the lead database with keyword filters, location filters, and other criteria.

Positive filter required: send at least one of positiveKeywords, nameIncludeTerms, urlIncludeTerms, crawledUrlIncludeTerms or descriptionIncludeTerms. Without one the call returns 200 with an empty leads array, requiresKeywords: true and a message, and charges nothing. Uses a two-phase filtering model: Phase 1 (Include) combines all positive keywords with OR logic, Phase 2 (Exclude) removes matches via AND logic.

Credit System (credit plans: Starter, Growth, Scale, Platinum, Enterprise): each new lead returned costs 1 credit. Charging is sticky: a lead you have already received through any channel (dashboard, API, MCP or email schedule) is never charged again, even if its data changed later, and a new lead that shares a primary phone or primary email with a lead you already received is also free. Within the page selected by page and limit, new leads are always ordered first, and they are cut to the smaller of maxCredits and your spendable balance (credit balance plus any overage-budget headroom); when the balance was the limit the response carries X-Credits-Capped: true. Omitting maxCredits therefore caps the request at your spendable balance instead of failing. 402 insufficient_credits only happens if a concurrent request spends the balance between the check and the charge. creditsUsed and creditsRemaining in the response report what was charged. Your export blacklist is not applied to this endpoint (GET /leads/preview and POST /leads/export apply it).

Lead Database: queries run against the Main database ('other'), which contains businesses of all types (e.g., accounting firms, marketing agencies, medical practices) with both phone numbers and email addresses as available contact methods. The database parameter is kept for backward compatibility; any value resolves to the Main database.

Wildcard Pattern Matching: All keyword and term parameters support `*` as a wildcard character that matches any sequence of characters. For example, `*account*` matches 'accounting', 'accountant', 'accounting firm', etc. Multiple wildcards in a single term let you match compound phrases: `*book*keep*` matches 'bookkeeping', 'bookkeeper services', etc. Other examples: `*market*agency*`, `*tax*prep*`. Keywords without wildcards perform substring matching by default (equivalent to wrapping in `*...*`).

The call is also capped at your spendable balance (credit balance plus any overage-budget headroom), so the effective cap is the smaller of the two; when the balance was the limit the response carries X-Credits-Capped: true. Leads you already received are included free up to maxResults or the page limit. Set 0 to receive only leads you already received, at no cost. If omitted, the call is capped at your spendable balance.

get.summary: Preview leads with masked contact info (no credits)
get.description:
Preview leads matching your filters with masked contact details, at no credit cost. Accepts the same filters as GET /leads (including the contact term filters such as emailPrimaryInclude and phonePrimaryInclude, and the company-column include, exclude and empty filters) plus excludePurchased; maxCredits and maxResults do not apply. Use it to test filters and size a query before spending credits on GET /leads or POST /leads/export.

Masking: contact values are masked, not hashed. A phone keeps its area code and last two digits, for example '(512) ***-**42', and an email keeps its first three characters and the full domain, for example 'hel*@domain.com'. Total Phones, the email tier lists and founder emails and phones are masked value by value.

Leads you already received come back unmasked with contactExported: true, the same as on the dashboard. A lead counts as received when its id was delivered to you, or when its primary phone, Total Phones, primary email or Email Tier 1-6 values include the primary phone or primary email of a lead you already received. Charging is narrower (it compares primary phone and primary email only), so a lead revealed only through a Total Phones or Email Tier value can still cost a credit on GET /leads or POST /leads/export.

Set excludePurchased=true to drop leads you already received. They are removed after the page is selected, so a page can hold fewer than limit leads while pagination.total still counts them. Your export blacklist is applied. Response includes preview: true.

parameters.description: When true, omit leads you already received (by lead id or by a shared contact point, as described above) from the page. Default false.

post.description:
Export leads matching your filters (or specific selectedIds) as CSV, JSON or XLSX files. The file type comes from the export format (formatId, or your default format). Up to 100,000 leads per filter export. Rate limited to 5 exports per minute, shared with the other export endpoints and the email schedule trigger.

Credits (credit plans: Starter, Growth, Scale, Platinum, Enterprise): each new lead exported costs 1 credit. Charging is sticky: a lead you have already received through any channel (dashboard, API, MCP or email schedule) is never charged again, even if its data changed later, and a new lead that shares a primary phone or primary email with a lead you already received is also free. New leads are always ordered first, and they are cut to the smaller of maxCredits and your spendable balance (credit balance plus any overage-budget headroom); when the balance was the limit the response carries X-Credits-Capped: true. Omitting maxCredits therefore caps the request at your spendable balance instead of failing. 402 insufficient_credits only happens if a concurrent request spends the balance between the check and the charge.

File bodies: with inline true (the default) each file's data field holds the whole file, as plain UTF-8 text for csv and json files and as base64 for xlsx files. Set inline=false to receive download links instead, which is recommended for large exports. Every file is also kept in export history for 90 days.

XLSX is limited to 20,000 rows per file. Any xlsx export that would put more than 20,000 rows in one file returns 400 export_too_large: a single-file export, the largest part of a split format (maxRowsPerFile above 20,000 or not set, or equal_parts / parts_max_rows parts that come out larger), or the includeTotal file, which holds every row. That check runs after the leads are charged and recorded as received. Do not simply repeat the request: an export picks new leads first, so a repeat can charge for different leads. Re-run it with maxCredits 0 (and without excludePurchased) using a csv export format or an xlsx format with splitFiles true, splitMode max_rows, maxRowsPerFile of 20,000 or less and includeTotal false, which returns the leads you already have at no cost, or re-export them with POST /lead-export-history/re-export.

Default-format files name the buying-signal columns Last Buying Signal and Buying Signal Type (CSV/XLSX headers and JSON keys); they no longer have Last Updated / Update Reason columns. To keep the old header names, pass a formatId whose fieldMappings map lastUpdated and lastUpdatedReason to the names you need.

database.description: Lead database. Only 'other' (the Main database) is available. Kept for backward compatibility: legacy values are still accepted and resolve to the Main database.

filters.description: Same filter parameters as GET /leads (positiveKeywords, negativeKeywords, stateInclude, buyingSignalTypeFilter, lastBuyingSignalFrom, lastBuyingSignalTo, etc.). buyingSignalTypeFilter accepts a JSON array or a comma-separated string. The older names updateReasonFilter, lastUpdatedFrom and lastUpdatedTo are still accepted (ignored when the new name is also sent).

selectedIds.description: Specific lead IDs to export (alternative to filters)

formatId.description: Export format template ID. Uses default format if not specified.

maxLeads.description: Most leads to include in this export. Leads over the cap, and new leads cut by the credit cap, are counted in overflowCount and kept in the lead reservoir while it has room, then added to your next export that also sets maxLeads. The reservoir is one pool per account, shared with your email schedules and capped at your plan's monthly credit allowance; leads that do not fit are not kept. If omitted, all matching leads are exported, subject to the credit cap.

maxResults.description: Most leads in this export, new leads plus leads you already received. New leads come first. If omitted, all matching leads are included, subject to the credit cap.

maxCredits.description: Most credits to spend on this export. Only new leads count. The export is also capped at your spendable balance (credit balance plus any overage-budget headroom), so the effective cap is the smaller of the two; when the balance was the limit the response carries X-Credits-Capped: true. Leads you already received are included free up to maxResults. Set 0 to export only leads you already received, at no cost. If omitted, the export is capped at your spendable balance.

excludePurchased.description: When true, export only leads you have not received yet. Leads you already received (matched by lead id, or by a shared contact point as described on GET /leads/preview) are skipped before export. Charging rules are unchanged. Default false.

inline.description: When false, each entry in the response `files` array omits its `data` (the whole file body) and carries `exportId` plus `downloadUrl` instead, so you fetch the bytes from GET /export-history/{id}/download when you want them. Recommended for large exports: a 100,000-row export inlined as JSON can be tens of megabytes that most clients write straight to disk anyway. `fileName`, `fileType` and `size` are always present either way. May also be supplied as the query parameter ?inline=false. Default true, which is the original response shape. A file that could not be saved to export history keeps its `data` and has no `downloadUrl`.

parameters.name: inline
parameters.description: Same as the `inline` body property, for clients that prefer it on the query string. When false the response omits each file's `data` and returns `exportId` + `downloadUrl` instead. A file that could not be saved to export history keeps its `data` and has no `downloadUrl`.

data.description: The whole file body, present when inline is true (the default): plain UTF-8 text for csv and json files, base64-encoded bytes for xlsx files. With inline=false it is omitted, except for a file that could not be saved to export history: that file comes back here instead, with no downloadUrl, so a paid export is never lost.

size.description: File size in bytes (for xlsx, the size of the decoded file)

exportId.description: This file's own export-history id. Present only when inline=false. A split export writes one history row PER FILE, so this - not the top-level exportId, which is only the first - is what addresses parts 2..N.

downloadUrl.description: Relative path to fetch this file's bytes: /api/v1/export-history/{exportId}/download. Present only when inline=false and the file was saved to export history, where it can be downloaded for 90 days.

databaseType.description: The lead database that served this request: always 'other' (the Main database).

creditsUsed.description: Number of credits deducted for net-new leads (credit-plan users only)

creditsRemaining.description: Remaining credit balance after this export (credit-plan users only)

maxLeads.description: Echo of maxLeads parameter (only present when maxLeads was specified)

overflowCount.description: Leads left out of this export by maxLeads or by the credit cap (only present when maxLeads is specified). They are kept in your account's lead reservoir while it has room (one pool shared with your email schedules, up to your plan's monthly credit allowance); leads that do not fit are not kept.

maxCredits.description: Echo of maxCredits parameter (only present when maxCredits was specified)

post.description: Upgrade or downgrade your subscription plan. Available target plans: starter, growth, scale. Downgrades take effect at renewal: credits stay usable until the renewal date, then the remaining balance (unused, rolled-over, and purchased credits) expires and the new plan's allocation is granted. While a downgrade is pending, moving back to your original plan (or a higher plan) before renewal voids it and keeps your credits (changeType 'upgrade', charged now); choosing another plan that is still below your original plan changes the pending downgrade (changeType 'downgrade', no charge), and the expiry still applies at renewal. During a free trial, mode 'switch_trial' (the default) changes the plan with no charge and keeps the trial end date; the trial has one spend counter, so credits already used stay used and creditsRemaining is 50% of the new plan minus what was used, never below zero. Mode 'activate_now' ends the trial, charges the target plan now, grants its full monthly allocation, and carries that plan's remaining trial allowance (50% of the plan minus what was used) into the rolling credit balance as permanentCreditsAdded.
